title: Government's Plans in our Continued Fight against COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Government's Plans in our Continued Fight against COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: Economic impact and fiscal measures
sections.summary: As virus measures ease, the economic impact must be faced, after nearly $100 billion in fiscal measures cushioned it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Now, as we emerge from the various measures to curb the spread of the virus, we will have to face the stark reality of its economic impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: So far, we been somewhat cushioned by the major fiscal measures announced by the Government – amounting to nearly $100 billion and 20% of our GDP.

sections.label: MTI economic contraction forecast
sections.summary: MTI expects the economy to contract by 4% to 7% this year, with significant downside risks remaining.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Based on the latest data, MTI expects our economy to contract by 4% to 7% this year, and there remain significant downside risks.

sections.label: ICT sector first quarter growth
sections.summary: In the first quarter of this year, the ICT sector expanded by 3.5% with 1,100 new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In the first quarter of this year, the ICT sector expanded by 3.5% with 1,100 new jobs.

sections.label: Training Singaporeans in tech jobs
sections.summary: Leading tech and non-tech companies will partner to place and train 3,000 Singaporeans in tech jobs over two to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In other words, we will partner leading tech and non-tech companies to place and train 3,000 Singaporeans in good tech jobs over the next two to three years – in functions like digital marketing, software engineering, cybersecurity and data analytics.

sections.label: Digital Resilience Bonus Scheme payments
sections.summary: Foreword Coffee adopted digital ordering and plans more solutions, earning $2,500 more under the Digital Resilience Bonus Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To advance its digitalisation journey, Foreword Coffee’s owner Mr Lim Wei Jie adopted a digital ordering solution and he also plans to deploy HR, payroll and accounting solutions in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: That will entitle the company to an additional $2,500 under the Digital Resilience Bonus Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Businesses that already have basic digital capabilities will receive an additional $5,000 should they decide to adopt advanced digital solutions like data mining and data analytics.

sections.label: Hawker e-payment adoption effort
sections.summary: A multi-agency effort will help over 18,000 stallholders adopt e-payment solutions by mid-next year, with bonuses for eligible hawkers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In this multi-agency effort by IMDA, Enterprise Singapore, NEA, JTC and HDB, we will reach out to and help over 18,000 stallholders adopt e-payment solutions by the middle of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Hawkers who sign up for the unified e-payment solution and fulfil the minimum transaction requirements will receive a bonus of up to $300 per month over five months.

sections.label: Government digital journey pledge
sections.summary: The Government says it will leave no one behind and walk the digital journey with Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To them I say, on behalf of the Government, we will leave no one behind and will walk this digital journey with you.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: So, let us come together, seize this opportunity fully and secure a bright digital future for each and every Singaporean.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget $33 billion
sections.summary: The Fortitude Budget sets aside a further $33 billion to sustain livelihoods and give businesses a lifeline.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In the Fortitude Budget, a further $33 billion is set aside to ensure livelihoods are broadly sustained and it seeks to provide a lifeline for businesses to resume in small steps.

sections.label: Trade classification for business resumption
sections.summary: The rationale for allowing one trade to open in Phase One but not a similar one raised questions on MTI's classification.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, the trade classification on resumption of business after circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: It is understandable why the need for us to re-open in three phases but the rationale of why one trade is allowed to open in Phase One while another quite similar in nature is not allowed to do so had raised brows on how MTI decided the trade classification for business resumption.

sections.label: Fortnightly swab tests for workers
sections.summary: Testing capacity and rapid results, not cost, may be the bottleneck; only over 10% of foreign workers were tested.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Citing one of the new measures on mandating workers to be sent for swab test every fortnight before they are allowed on the work site, cost being one concern, but the ability to have enough testing and rapid results made available would likely be the bottleneck in the months ahead.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Based on current test rate, we only managed to test over 10% of the total foreign worker population mainly residing in the dormitories.

sections.label: Safe Management Officers training slots
sections.summary: Feedback cites insufficient BCA training slots until early July, prompting suggestions for mass online training and certification.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: On this note of digitalisation, I would like to ask the Minister about the Safe Management Officers mandated training by BCA.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: There is ground feedback of insufficient training slots available until early July.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Given the pervasiveness of technology and the ease of setting virtual meetings, is it not possible for several mass online training sessions to be conducted for workers even if they do not belong to the same company?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Also, if there is a need for certifications, the workers who are trained can individually do the assessments online using their mobile phones and be certified via these platforms.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget job loss estimates
sections.summary: Economists and analysts say Fortitude Budget schemes may contain full-year job losses to around 100,000 to 150,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Some economists and analysts highlight that the Fortitude Budget schemes will help to contain the job losses to around 100,000 to 150,000 or less – down from earlier estimates of about 150,000 to 200,000 – for the full year.

sections.label: Help for middle-aged Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage notes 4,000 traineeships, enhanced hiring incentives and the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package aiming to create close to 100,000 opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am glad to see that more help and support have been made available for middle-aged Singaporeans through the 4,000 traineeships and enhanced hiring incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There is also the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package that aims to create close to 100,000 jobs, traineeships and skills training opportunities.

sections.label: Tax filing deadline extension
sections.summary: The tax filing deadline was extended to 31 May 2020, and the speaker hopes the Government considers further deferring it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The tax filing deadline has been extended to 31 May 2020 but I hope that the Government can consider further deferring this timeline, considering that this is still a developing situation.

sections.label: Support for small landlords
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will look at individual circumstances of small landlords and offer support through higher property tax rebates or longer bank mortgage deferments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But it is a double blow to have to forgo a two-month rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can continue to look at the individual circumstances of some of these small landlords, and offer them support through higher property tax rebates, or even through longer bank mortgage deferments.

sections.label: Fourth Budget fiscal support
sections.summary: The fourth Budget set aside S$33 billion, bringing total fiscal support to $93 billion, about 20% of GDP, with $13 billion in the Contingencies Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government set aside another S$33 billion in the fourth Budget this year, with a big focus on helping firms stay afloat and creating jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This brings the total fiscal support to $93 billion, about 20% of GDP, placing Singapore as among the top spenders in this global pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Out of the $33 billion, $13 billion was set aside in the Contingencies Fund, which the Government can draw from in the case of unforeseen developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is more than seven times, in terms of fiscal deficit, estimated in the first Unity Budget which was about $10.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Going forward, to ensure sufficient buffer, the Singapore Government is required to maintain a balanced Budget over each term of Government under the Constitution.

sections.label: Drawing down fiscal reserves
sections.summary: The Government can keep tapping its fiscal reserves, of which $52 billion has been drawn, but risks depleting its war chest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government can keep on tapping and running down its fiscal reserves, of which $52 billion has already been drawn and counting but runs the risk of depleting its war chest.

sections.label: FY2021 fiscal deficit outlook
sections.summary: The fiscal deficit in FY2021 will likely remain large as recovery is gradual, with the 10-year SGS bond yield at 0.8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The fiscal deficit in FY2021 will likely remain large, as any economic recovery will be very gradual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The 10-year SGS bond yield is currently trading at 0.8%.
